Very polite and friendly staff. I had made an appointment for my toy poodle to be groomed. She is a senior dog and have become quite aggressive when it came time to cut her.
She was at the point where she wouldn’t even let me brush her at home. I discussed with the staff at the facility about her aggression and the possibility of her being able to Be groomed the staff was very informative and very knowledgeable with senior dogs and aggression. They said they would do everything to make the experience comfortable for her and if she became too agitated, they could do a cut under mild sedation that was great. In conclusion, my toy poodle got cut wash, trimmed nails, clipped all without sedation all because of her groomer Joshua he was excellent, very professional very caring. I have nothing but good things to say about this place before I left. I made sure I made another appointment for my little Minky to be seen again by Josha
We are grateful for you. Thank you for allowing us to care for your pet and for taking the time to share thoughts about your experience.

Do NOT recommend this business to anyone!
I took my dog in for a simple grooming… bath and brush, not even a cut or style or anything. They charged me $250 and stated that my dog (a female GSD who weighed 85lbs at her last vet visit two months ago) weighed 94lbs. This is highway robbery! On top of that, the lady who groomed her was sick.
Upon paying the asinine amount and asking for a detailed invoice, they emailed me the invoice… which stated that they had scheduled her for another grooming appointment in the future without my consent! I am glad I noticed it on my invoice, because otherwise they would have charged me for a grooming appointment that I did NOT make on the day of when I didn’t show up (because they are the ones who made the appointment without my knowledge).

This is not the correct way to run a business. Extremely overpriced and shady business practices. Would not recommend and would give zero stars if that were an option.

These people forget this is still north Philly I don’t care what fancy name u cover it with , just overcharging and acting like you are above is outrageous. And that’s how my experience here feels.

And suggested if I wanted an estimate I should go somewhere else.

I check my invoice and then I got charged 1 year rabies shot!!! I texted/communicated to them that I got the wrong rabies shot and they told me it’s because of the Feline Injection-Site Sarcoma. But it’s not what I asked for. This miscommunication required me to come again which is very distressing for my cat. They did comp the tech visit and rabies shot but the visit and 3 years rabies shot (equivalent cost of 1 year rabies shot) was TOTALLY unnecessary! I chose to bring my cat here since my regular vet had no last minute openings when I needed one. The care from the kind vet was great, but the overall communication is lacking significantly. The company has a mainly text-based model. You might think that this would result in easy, fast communication, but that is not the case. Up to 36 hours to get test results? Mine came in at the 38th hour, after I followed up multiple times. The vet recommended an RX diet, but after I figured out what food I needed and asked for an authorization, 2 days passed before a reply. Finally they replied that in order to buy the food from Chewy (i.e. the more affordable option), you have to go to their location and pick up a physical RX (I thought they did things digitally?). Otherwise, you can order it through *their* system. I interpret this as they want to make more off of patients and don't care if it inconveniences them or costs them more money.

After your first visit here you will be spammed with "refer a friend and get $50!" emails and texts, yet you won't get a reply from the front desk if you email them and the vet (again, who I like) isn't especially responsive either. I don't blame them, I blame the company. I didn't expect much from a chain vet, but unfortunately I've gotten wrapped up in an inefficient system that isn't great for animals or owners. P.S. you have to call to get records of test results--they have a portal, yet they don't automatically post them or email them for some reason? Please stop giving pet owners more work when they are stressed out.

We brought our kitten Niko to Heart & Paw after he ingested a key ring and was diagnosed with anemia and toxic metal poisoning. While the staff did provide some supportive care (fluids, likely activated charcoal, and possibly an enema), we ultimately feel that a major failure in communication and documentation played a role in his tragic passing.

Due to financial constraints, we couldn’t afford the $10,000+ blood transfusion that was offered as the primary treatment option. We weren’t given much reassurance about his chances with either option, but went with supportive care, hoping it would stabilize him.

The biggest issue came at discharge. The veterinarian who treated Niko didn’t speak with us directly again. Instead, a tech we’d never met handed him back with brief home instructions and told us we’d receive a full medical summary by email. That summary never came—despite us following up multiple times.

Because we didn’t have documentation of what treatments or tests had been done, we delayed taking him to the emergency vet, waiting for the promised records to avoid paying twice for the same procedures. On Saturday, when we finally rushed him to the ER, Niko seized and died in my daughter’s arms on the way there.

We’re devastated. We feel that had we been given his medical records promptly at discharge—something that should be routine—we could have made more informed decisions and gotten him emergency care sooner. Instead, we left with a non-itemized bill and no follow-up from the vet.

This isn’t about blame. It’s about accountability and the need for better discharge procedures. Pet parents deserve proper communication, especially when they’re trying to balance urgent medical care with financial realities. Niko deserved better. So did we.

A Disappointing Experience with Room for Improvement

I initially chose Heart and Paw for my dog, Pepper, after thoroughly researching their reputation and services. My early visits started off positively, with kind and professional interactions from the front desk staff and other team members, which gave me confidence in their care.

However, my experience took a disappointing turn. During one visit, a staff member displayed unprofessional behavior, avoiding eye contact and providing vague answers. Concerned, I raised the issue with the receptionist, expecting it to be addressed. Unfortunately, when I followed up, I received a response that felt dismissive and one-sided, as though my concerns were not taken seriously.

A particularly upsetting moment occurred during a phone call when I inquired why there was no follow-up to check on Pepper’s condition after spending over $1,000 on an ultrasound, examination, and lifelong special food. I suggested even a basic questionnaire for clients, but the response I received was, "We have over 1,000 clients, we can't call everyone," or words to that effect. This response felt unprofessional and dismissive, especially considering the significant investment I made in Pepper's care.

Pepper is not just a pet; he is a beloved companion to my 100-year-old father, and their bond is incredibly meaningful to our family. I trusted Heart and Paw based on my research and was willing to make financial sacrifices to ensure Pepper’s well-being. While Pepper's care has improved, the lack of follow-up and dismissive communication left me feeling undervalued as a client.

I hope Heart and Paw considers implementing a more thoughtful approach to client follow-up and customer service. Even a small gesture, like a post-visit questionnaire, would go a long way in showing clients that their concerns are valued. While some aspects of their care are commendable, my experience highlights the need for consistency and improvement.
